correctness.rationale: Fourier characters diagonalize every line-sum normal block with exact weight w_d; primitive frequencies isolate one d (least eigenvalue), while prime-local high-valuation frequencies realize any residue-fiber W_p,ell (greatest). No nonzero Fourier mode exceeds a prime fiber. Averaging residue fibers at the least prime proves the sharp lower ratio; min equals mean only for uniform weights. Prime-power CRT counts determine all remaining eigenvalues and multiplicities. CHECK.py enumerated all moduli N=2..30 with independent weighted Fourier-block and direct Gram checks. Mathematical proof holds all N and w>0; finite experiments alone do not prove it.

originality.rationale: The weighted positive scalar-view minimax on all composite cyclic grids, its exact two spectral endpoints, and unique flat equality case are not stated by the material actually inspected. Beylkin offers general periodic Fourier-block inversions; Kingston–Svalbe establish projective lines and sampling redundancy; Kingston describes orthogonal projection bases; later work uses frequency-dependent filtering. Prior work supplies ingredients, but these statements are not identical to the constrained all-N minimax and the exact weighted endpoints. Major limitation: relevant publisher full texts remain unavailable and could contain an equivalent statement; priority is not exhaustively certified.

value.rationale: Scalar-per-view weighting is a natural restricted acquisition model, distinct from frequency-filtering inversion. Exact frame bounds and a rigid least-prime arithmetic obstruction for every composite cyclic resolution decide the best possible conditioning in this class and give full unweighted noise-amplification spectrum; this is structurally motivated and not an arbitrary numerical slice.
